html:
An American company formed in 1899 that grew and shipped bananas from Central America and the Caribbean. It held so much power over small states that it gave rise to the term banana republic.

It owned huge plantations in Guatemala, Honduras, Costa Rica, Colombia, Panama and Cuba, along with railways, ports, telegraph lines and a fleet of refrigerated ships. In several countries it was the biggest landowner and employer. Its critics called it "the octopus".

It often got its way by bribing politicians and calling on the US government. Its darkest moments:

  • 1928: the Colombian army killed striking banana workers in the Banana Massacre, later retold in One Hundred Years of Solitude.
  • 1954: after Guatemala's elected president Jacobo Árbenz took unused company land for land reform, the CIA organised a coup that overthrew him.

In 1970 it merged into United Brands, which later became Chiquita.
